S79.01.needs: a signed-in AGI account (Auto is greyed out when signed out)
S79.01.note: The app does not show which model answered a request on these screens, so the tester can only check that Auto is selected and the answer arrives.
steps: Open a new chat in the AGI VS Code panel and read the model pill.
Confirm the pill says Auto and that Auto is the first row under Recommended when you click it.
Type a short question and send it.
Check that the answer arrives and the pill still says Auto, with no model picked by you. Compare with Expected: Auto picks a model for each request.
S79.01.where: Model pill (the word Auto under the chat box) > Recommended > Auto

S79.02.needs: a signed-in AGI account; a local model in Ollama or LM Studio for the On this device group (optional)
S79.02.note: I confirmed the pill and the Code: Select Model command; I did not confirm the label of each cloud provider group.
steps: Click the model pill above the chat box.
Choose a named model from the list (for example one under On this device if a local model is running, or another listed model).
Send a short message.
Check that the pill now shows the model you chose, and that the answer comes back. Compare with Expected: the request runs on the model you picked.
S79.02.where: Model pill > click a named model (not Auto); or Command Palette > Code: Select Model

labels.text: Code: Use Project in This Chat

S79.03.needs: a signed-in account with at least one project
S79.03.note: The code offers the default model as a choice when the project is used; I did not confirm that every new chat in the project starts on it without that step.
steps: Run Code: Show Projects from the Command Palette.
Open a project with Code: Open Project.
Click Default model in the project list and pick a model (or No default model to clear it).
Run Code: Use Project in This Chat and start a new chat; compare the model pill with Expected. If the pill differs, a message offers Choose the model.
S79.03.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Projects > open a project > Default model

S79.04.needs: a signed-in AGI account on a plan that includes the Best profile
S79.04.note: Expected says premium for coding and reasoning, but the row is called Best and its description reads The most capable model your plan includes, for harder work. The task-type choice is inner and not shown.
steps: Click the model pill.
Under Recommended, choose Auto · Best.
Send a coding or reasoning question.
Check that the pill keeps Auto · Best and the answer arrives. Compare with Expected: a task-specific profile is applied.

S79.05.note: The row is called Instant, and its description reads Answers fastest, on the quickest models your plan includes.
steps: Click the model pill.
Under Recommended, choose Auto · Instant.
Send a short question.
Check that the pill keeps Auto · Instant and the answer comes back quickly. Compare with Expected: the fastest eligible route is used.

S79.06.needs: a signed-in AGI account on a plan that includes the Best profile
S79.06.note: The Best row is the same row as S79.04; the code has one quality profile for both.
steps: Click the model pill.
Under Recommended, choose Auto · Best.
Send a harder question.
Check that the pill keeps Auto · Best and the answer arrives. Compare with Expected: the most capable eligible route is used.

S79.07.note: The row is called Economy, and its description reads The lowest-cost model that can handle the task.
steps: Click the model pill.
Under Recommended, choose Auto · Economy.
Send a simple question.
Check that the pill keeps Auto · Economy and the answer arrives. Compare with Expected: the cheapest eligible route is used.

S79.08.needs: a local model running in Ollama or LM Studio (for the nearest control)
S79.08.note: No privacy-first profile is in the Auto rows (only Auto, Instant, Best, Economy). The nearest visible controls are the On this device group in the model pill and the trust-boundary warning in Code: Select Model. Searched the model-picker folder and the routing profile list for privacy.

S79.09.note: Intent classification runs in the chat state code for each message when Auto is selected, with no control or label of its own.
S79.09.where: Inner routing step; its effect is only seen through which model Auto uses

S79.10.note: Tool needs are classified per request with no control of their own; the Browse the web toggle is a separate manual control.
S79.10.where: Inner routing step; its effect is only seen through the answer

S79.11.needs: an image file and a signed-in AGI account
S79.11.note: The exact label of the plus control was not confirmed; the menu is labelled Add context.
steps: Click the plus control in the chat box and choose an image under Add context.
Send a question about the image.
Check that the answer describes the image instead of saying it cannot see one. Compare with Expected: the request is sent to a model that accepts images.
S79.11.where: Seen when an image is attached in the chat box: the answer should describe the image

S79.12.note: Complexity is classified per request with no visible label; the effort setting is a separate control.
S79.12.where: Inner classification; no screen shows the complexity level

S79.13.note: The code detects fresh-information requests without a control. The Browse the web toggle is manual and is not the automatic detection Expected describes.
S79.13.where: Inner detection; the manual control is Browse the web in the plus menu

S79.14.note: The pill list greys rows; the lock icon appears in the Code: Select Model list.
steps: Sign out, or use an account with no plan, then open the model pill.
Look for greyed Auto rows and any Needs setup on this machine section.
Open Command Palette > Code: Select Model and check that unavailable rows show a lock.
Compare with Expected: unavailable models are not offered as choices that fail.
S79.14.where: Model pill list: greyed rows and the Needs setup on this machine section

S79.15.note: Route ranking by health, cost and cache is server and runtime logic with no visible control.
S79.15.where: Inner provider-route choice; no screen shows the chosen route

S79.16.needs: a signed-in account; a route that fails (for example a spent free allowance) to see the card
S79.16.note: The code keeps the chosen model; I did not confirm an end-to-end failure that keeps the same model.
steps: Pick a named model in the model pill.
Send a message.
If the turn fails, read the failure card; it offers Switch model, and the chat does not switch by itself.
If you pick a model that would lose something, read the Switch to <model>? prompt and its Switch anyway button. Compare with Expected: the chosen model is not replaced silently.
S79.16.where: Model pill > click a named model (not Auto), then send a message that fails

S79.19.needs: a Free account with a spent allowance
S79.19.note: Budget-aware choice of route is inner logic; only the resulting failure card is visible.
steps: Use up the free allowance on a Free account, or hit a plan limit.
Send a message.
Read the failure card and check that it offers Switch model or names a reset time. Compare with Expected: routing accounts for the remaining budget.
S79.19.where: Seen only when the free allowance or plan limit is spent: the failure card offers Switch model

S79.20.needs: a route that fails (for example a provider with no credit)
S79.20.note: Health-based demotion is inner; the visible part is the card and its offer.
steps: Cause a route failure, for example a provider with no credit.
Read the failure card.
Click Continue with <model> if it is shown, and check the turn is sent again on another model. Compare with Expected: failed calls fall back to a healthy alternative.
S79.20.where: Seen on a failed turn: the failure card offers Continue with <model> and Switch model

S79.21.needs: a route failure, for example a spent free allowance
S79.21.note: Switch model opens the model list rather than switching in one click; the one-click path is Continue with <model>, shown only when the failure names an alternative.
steps: Cause a route failure, for example a spent free allowance.
Read the red failure card.

Click Switch model and check that the model list opens. If the card instead shows Continue with <model>, click it and check the turn is resent on that model. Compare with Expected: a one-click switch is offered.
S79.21.where: Chat failure card > Switch model (opens the model list)

S79.30.note: The fallback itself is inner logic in the routing code; the visible part is that the default is Auto.
steps: Open a new chat and do not change the model pill.
Check the pill reads Auto.
Send a plain message and check an answer arrives. Compare with Expected: an unclear request falls back to a safe default.
S79.30.where: Model pill shows Auto as the default
